lab_title: Apparent Retrograde Motion of Outer Planets
top_level_objectives: Explain apparent retrograde motion from an Earth-centered perspective.
Explain apparent retrograde motion from a Sun-centered perspective.
Compare the retrograde motion of different outer planets (Mars, Jupiter, Saturn).
Articulate why apparent retrograde motion was key evidence for the heliocentric model.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the phenomenon of retrograde motion as observed from Earth.
key_visuals: A view of the night sky with constellations.
Mars shown as a distinct point of light moving against the stars.
student_actions: Observe the nightly eastward motion of Mars against the background stars.
Observe Mars slow down, reverse direction (westward motion), and then resume eastward motion over a simulated period of weeks.

scenes.brief_purpose: Illustrate the complexity of explaining retrograde motion with a purely geocentric model.
key_visuals: Earth at the center of the solar system.
Mars shown with an epicycle and deferent to explain its retrograde path.
student_actions: Attempt to trace the path of Mars using the epicycle/deferent system.
Recognize the difficulty and contrivance of this model in reproducing Mars's observed motion.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the heliocentric model with planets in simple circular orbits.
key_visuals: Earth and Mars shown in separate, roughly circular orbits around the Sun.
student_actions: Observe the smooth, independent, counter-clockwise motion of Earth and Mars around the Sun.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate how relative motion in the heliocentric model causes apparent retrograde motion.
key_visuals: The Sun, Earth, and Mars in orbit.
A viewpoint from outside the solar system.
A "ghost" or projected path of Mars as seen from Earth.
student_actions: Observe the solar system from a distant viewpoint.
Slow down or pause time to see Earth overtake Mars on its inner orbit.
Notice how Mars appears to move backward against the background stars only during the overtaking period.

scenes.brief_purpose: Compare the retrograde motion of Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.
key_visuals: The Sun, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn in their respective orbits.
Visual indicators showing the apparent retrograde path of each outer planet as seen from Earth.
student_actions: Observe the relative speeds and orbital distances of Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.
Compare the duration and angular extent of the retrograde loops for each planet.
Note that outer planets farther from the Sun exhibit less pronounced retrograde motion.

scenes.brief_purpose: Reinforce the significance of retrograde motion as evidence for the heliocentric model.
key_visuals: Side-by-side comparison of the geocentric (with epicycles) and heliocentric explanations for Mars's motion.
Text highlighting the simplicity and explanatory power of the heliocentric model.
student_actions: Reflect on the observations from previous scenes.
Conclude why the heliocentric model provides a more natural and accurate explanation for apparent retrograde motion.
